title: First token: service work versus client arrival
question: Which event ends prefill, and which event ends client TTFT?
scope: Three output tokens on a declared schematic event axis. Coordinates are illustrative, not measured latency. Transport buffering is shown explicitly.

steps.title: Request enters the service queue
steps.explanation: No output has been sampled or delivered.

snapshot.result: The client is waiting before the service reads the prompt.

steps.title: Finish queueing
steps.explanation: The request can now begin prompt processing.

snapshot.result: Queueing has ended; prompt processing has not.

transition.meaning: The request can now begin prompt processing.

steps.title: Prefill produces initial logits
steps.explanation: Prefill reads the prompt and produces the logits used for the first sample.

snapshot.result: Prefill has finished, but the client has no token yet.

transition.meaning: Prefill reads the prompt and produces the logits used for the first sample.

steps.title: Sample the first token
steps.explanation: Sampling turns the initial logits into t1; the client is still waiting.

snapshot.result: The first token exists at the service, while client TTFT continues.

transition.meaning: Sampling turns the initial logits into t1; the client is still waiting.

steps.title: Deliver the first token
steps.explanation: The first arrival ends client TTFT after queueing, prefill, sampling, and delivery.

snapshot.result: The first delivery ends client TTFT; later generation is still ahead.

transition.meaning: The first arrival ends client TTFT after queueing, prefill, sampling, and delivery.

steps.title: Generate the second token
steps.explanation: One subsequent generation pass produces t2; transport retains it.

snapshot.result: The second token remains buffered instead of arriving immediately.

transition.meaning: One subsequent generation pass produces t2; transport retains it.

steps.title: Generate the third token
steps.explanation: A second subsequent pass produces t3; neither later token has arrived yet.

snapshot.result: Distinct generation passes have produced both buffered later tokens.

transition.meaning: A second subsequent pass produces t3; neither later token has arrived yet.

steps.title: Deliver the buffered later tokens
steps.explanation: Transport delivers t2 and t3 in one chunk; arrivals conceal the separate generation passes.

snapshot.result: One client arrival carries tokens from separate service passes.

transition.meaning: Transport delivers t2 and t3 in one chunk; arrivals conceal the separate generation passes.

invariants: Prefill supplies the logits for the first token; later output tokens each require a subsequent pass.
Sampling and client receipt are distinct events.
A chunk can carry multiple tokens without merging their service generation passes.

title: Reject locally, cancel remotely

steps.title: Stream starts
steps.explanation: The runtime holds every partial proposal until validation completes.

snapshot.result: The local gate holds an incomplete proposal.

steps.title: Receive an open object
steps.explanation: The prefix is incomplete but still completable; no tool call is authorized.

snapshot.result: An open object remains completable and cannot be dispatched.

transition.meaning: The prefix is incomplete but still completable; no tool call is authorized.

steps.title: Receive a permitted key
steps.explanation: A permitted key still does not make the partial proposal dispatchable.

snapshot.result: The permitted key preserves completable parser state, not dispatch permission.

transition.meaning: A permitted key still does not make the partial proposal dispatchable.

steps.title: Reject an unknown key
steps.explanation: The received force key is absent from this declared schema. The local gate rejects the proposal.

snapshot.result: The unknown key closes the dispatch gate before remote cancellation.

transition.meaning: The received force key is absent from this declared schema. The local gate rejects the proposal.

steps.title: Send the cancellation request
steps.explanation: Sending a signal does not prove that the remote generation loop stopped.

snapshot.result: Remote decoding may still continue after the cancel signal leaves.

transition.meaning: Sending a signal does not prove that the remote generation loop stopped.

steps.title: Honor cancellation
steps.explanation: Acknowledgment stops future generation before KV release.

snapshot.result: Acknowledgment stops generation while service state remains allocated.

transition.meaning: Acknowledgment stops future generation before KV release.

steps.title: Release service KV state
steps.explanation: The request has no remaining service consumer; its private state can be freed.

snapshot.result: Service state is free; the rejected diagnostic prefix remains.

transition.meaning: The request has no remaining service consumer; its private state can be freed.

invariants: No incomplete or rejected proposal reaches tool dispatch.
Only the service can stop its decode loop and release its execution state.
The rejected diagnostic prefix remains available after service memory is released.

title: Where search retains and prunes state

scope: Declared candidate labels and toy scorer values, without any accuracy claim. Cases are distinct search procedures, not equal-budget performance comparisons. snapshot.result: The prompt yields two initial prefixes in one expansion.

title: Share a prefix, privatize a tail
question: Which KV entries must be copied before a fork appends?
scope: The source’s ten-token prefix, four-token blocks, tables [3,7,9], and private block 14. Full blocks 3 and 7 are summarized by their table entries; only tails are expanded. Tail sequences distinguish unwritten null entries from valid KV; the ownership register records whether the physical block is allocated.

steps.title: Candidate A retains the original tail
steps.explanation: Full blocks 3 and 7 and the initialized tail at block 9 belong to A.

snapshot.result: The original tail has valid entries followed by unwritten capacity.

steps.title: Resolve logical position 9
steps.explanation: Integer division selects the table entry; modulo selects the initialized slot.

snapshot.result: The selected table entry locates the block; the remainder locates its slot.

transition.meaning: Integer division selects the table entry; modulo selects the initialized slot.

steps.title: Fork B by sharing the prefix
steps.explanation: Both candidates reference the existing blocks; no KV entry has been copied.

snapshot.result: Both tables reference one original tail without duplicating its initialized KV.

transition.meaning: Both candidates reference the existing blocks; no KV entry has been copied.

steps.title: Reserve private block 14 for B
steps.explanation: The private tail is allocated before any initialized entry is copied.

private.status: Allocated to B; all entries unwritten

lookup.value: Private block 14: allocated to B; source slot 1

snapshot.result: B owns an empty private block; no copied KV is readable there yet.

transition.meaning: The private tail is allocated before any initialized entry is copied.

steps.title: Copy initialized tail entries
steps.explanation: Copy only positions 8 and 9. Unwritten capacity remains null; the source tail survives.

lookup.value: Private block 14: allocated to B; source slot 1

snapshot.result: The private tail now contains the initialized source entries; the source remains intact.

transition.meaning: Copy only positions 8 and 9. Unwritten capacity remains null; the source tail survives.

steps.title: Remap only B’s tail table entry
steps.explanation: B now resolves its tail to the initialized private copy; A still resolves to block 9.

lookup.value: Private block 14: allocated to B; source slot 1

snapshot.result: Only B changes its mapping, leaving A’s original tail reachable.

transition.meaning: B now resolves its tail to the initialized private copy; A still resolves to block 9.

steps.title: Append position 10 to B’s private tail
steps.explanation: The append initializes one free entry without modifying A’s original tail.

lookup.value: Private block 14: allocated to B; source slot 1

snapshot.result: B’s appended KV occupies its private tail while A’s sequence stays unchanged.

transition.meaning: The append initializes one free entry without modifying A’s original tail.

invariants: Candidate A’s table and original initialized entries survive B’s append.
Copy-on-write copies initialized tail entries only.
B’s table changes after its private copy is initialized, before its append.

title: Evict leaves before their ancestors

steps.title: Active paths coexist with dormant cache
steps.explanation: Root, Repair, and Test have an active request. Other remains internal while Final is retained.

snapshot.result: Dormant Other cannot be evicted while its Final child remains.

steps.title: Request free blocks
steps.explanation: The allocator requests three blocks; dormant internal nodes remain protected by their descendants.

snapshot.result: Allocator demand does not make a retained ancestor safe to evict.

transition.meaning: The allocator requests three blocks; dormant internal nodes remain protected by their descendants.

steps.title: Evict dormant leaf Final
steps.explanation: Final has no child and no execution reference. Remove its index entry and return its exclusive block.

snapshot.result: Removing Final exposes Other as a newly eligible leaf.

transition.meaning: Final has no child and no execution reference. Remove its index entry and return its exclusive block.

steps.title: Evict newly exposed leaf Other
steps.explanation: Other becomes a leaf only after Final disappears; it now has no retained descendant.

snapshot.result: Other can now disappear without breaking any retained path.

transition.meaning: Other becomes a leaf only after Final disappears; it now has no retained descendant.

steps.explanation: Rejected can be removed without touching the live Root–Repair–Test path.

snapshot.result: Only the active request path remains; dormant exclusive blocks are free.

invariants: No retained node loses its required ancestor.

Returning an exclusive block removes its physical pool occupancy.
